name: ASSO PIGLIATUTTO
description: Asso Pigliatutto ('Ace Takes All') is a variant of the classic Italian game Scopa. The defining twist is that playing an Ace allows a player to capture ALL cards on the table instantly. While it simplifies the math for beginners, it adds a layer of 'Ace-hoarding' strategy that changes the flow of the game significantly.

content.text: Asso Pigliatutto ('Ace Takes All') is a variant of the classic Italian game Scopa. The defining twist is that playing an Ace allows a player to capture ALL cards on the table instantly. While it simplifies the math for beginners, it adds a layer of 'Ace-hoarding' strategy that changes the flow of the game significantly.

Developed in Italy as a simplified or faster variation of Scopa. The name explicitly translates to 'Ace Takes All' (Pigliatutto). It is often taught to children as a gateway to standard Scopa because the Ace rule provides exciting, easy captures.
40-card Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Batons). If using a standard 52-card deck, remove 8s, 9s, and 10s. Kings=10, Queens=9, Jacks=8.
Dealer gives 3 cards to each player and places 4 cards face-up on the table. When players run out of cards, 3 more are dealt until the deck is empty.

items.text: Sbarazzino: Playing an Ace to sweep the table ALWAYS awards a Scopa point.
Napola (Naples): Additional points for capturing the Ace, Two, and Three of Coins (the 'Little Ladder').
